brief: JPM's midterm tracker argues that historical base rates (the sitting president's party has averaged ~27 House and ~3 Senate seat losses over 23 cycles) point to a Democratic House and Republican Senate, aligning with betting markets (48% GOP holds Senate, 86% Dems take House). Economy/affordability is the top voter issue, complicated by an unpopular Iran conflict: Houthi advances and attacks on Saudi's East-West pipeline pushed oil from $91.01 to $106 (+16.5%) since JPM's last note, and JPM says the resulting gas-price rise has significantly hurt Trump's economic approval. Senate math requires Democrats to flip 4 of the GOP's 53-47 majority, contested mainly in Alaska, Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas; the House is close (Cook Political Report: 197 Dem-likely vs 201 GOP-likely, 21 toss-ups). JPM's Joyce Chang expects a House flip that falls short of a full 'blue wave' given post-redistricting competitive-seat shrinkage, while Dubravko argues even a full Democratic sweep would still be checked by presidential veto and the Senate filibuster, constraining major Democratic legislation for two years; historically, gridlock has coincided with stronger S&P 500 returns than single-party control.
